name: Investor deck
notes: The version you send. Keep it separate from the version you present.

name: Deck appendix
notes: Detail that would slow the main deck: architecture, unit economics workings, competitive map.

name: One-pager / teaser
notes: What a warm introducer forwards. Must stand alone without you in the room.

name: Financial model
notes: Driver-based, with assumptions on their own tab and clearly labelled.

name: Historical financials
notes: P&L and bank statements to date.

name: Capitalisation table
notes: Current and pro-forma, including the option pool.

name: Prior financing documents
notes: Every SAFE, note and side letter issued to date.

name: Incorporation and governance documents
notes: Certificate of incorporation, bylaws, board consents.

name: IP assignment and contractor agreements
notes: Every founder, employee and contractor. The most common diligence gap.

name: Customer contracts and order forms
notes: Including any design-partner or pilot agreements.

name: Product demo recording
notes: Five minutes, no slides, real product.

name: Technical architecture overview
notes: How data flows from systems of record through decisioning to execution.

name: Product roadmap
notes: Next four quarters, tied to what each stage of autonomy requires.

name: Security and data handling overview
notes: Expect this early from anyone whose portfolio handles customer transaction data.

name: Market sizing and segmentation
notes: Bottom-up, with the assumptions visible.

name: Competitive landscape
notes: Include agencies, internal teams and platform-native automation - not only startups.

name: Platform risk memo
notes: The written answer to 'why will the platforms not do this themselves?'. Write it before you are asked.

name: Customer interviews and evidence log
notes: Every claim in the deck mapped to the evidence behind it.

name: Customer reference list
notes: Named references, with permission secured in advance.

name: Sales pipeline
notes: Current pipeline with stage and expected value.

name: Team bios and org plan
notes: Who is here, who you hire with this round, and why in that order.

name: Hiring plan
notes: Roles, timing and cost, reconciled with the financial model.
